title: Decision making underlying aggression and self-harm following social exclusion by friends: a hyperscanning study of borderline symptomatology
summary:
The study aims to investigate how the behavior of friends influences the decisions of patients with borderline personality disorder. More specifically, the objective is to understand the neuronal mechanisms behind aggression and self-harm in cases of social exclusion.
Therefore patients with borderline personality disorder will be examined using magnetic resonance imaging together with a healthy friend.
We expect that social exclusion leads to more aggression towards friends in patients with higher aggression traits while patients with lower aggression traits will display more self-harming behavoir.
We further take a dimensional approach by analysing changes in the aggression dynamics post-exclusion based on borderline symptomatology and not only on diagnosis, capturing also subclinical borderline traits in undiagnosed people.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All participants have no neurological disorders, normal or corrected-to-normal vision and are MRI-compatible.
The healthy participants must not have a mental disorder.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria for all participants include pregnancy, neurological disorders and MRI incompatibility. MRI incompatibility includes MRI incompatible implants or devices in the body, including metallic or magnetic implants containing iron, cobalt or nickel (e.g. pacemakers, automatic insulin pumps), implanted hearing aids [e.g. cochlear implants], metal endoprostheses, metal parts or metal splinters in the body and magnetically attached dental prostheses. Also excluded are people who suffer from claustrophobia and people with back problems that prevent  laying  in  the  scanner  for  the  duration  of  the experiment without experiencing pain.

Additional exclusion criteria for healthy test subjects are current psychiatric  or  neurological  illness, drug use, and psychoactive medication.
